guide.title: How to make a CSV file
guide.intro: Make a table like the one below in a spreadsheet app (Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers, …) and save it in CSV format.

notes.encoding: Use UTF-8. See "How to save as a UTF-8 CSV" below.
notes.duplicate: A word with the same characters, and the same pinyin (or no pinyin on either side), is treated as a duplicate of a saved word.
notes.json: JSON is for restoring files (backups) exported from this app.

guide.headerWarning: Spell the column names in the first row exactly like the English names in the table below (upper or lower case does not matter). Column names in Japanese or Chinese, such as "繁體字", cannot be read. If unsure, start from the "Template with column names only".
guide.templateHint: Open the template in a spreadsheet app, enter words from row 2, and save. You can delete the example words.

save.title: How to save as a UTF-8 CSV (Excel and others)
save.lead: Always save the CSV in UTF-8 so the characters are not garbled. Excel's "CSV (Comma delimited)" is not UTF-8 and cannot be read.

excelWindows.title: Excel (Windows)
steps: Choose File → Save As (or Save a Copy when AutoSave is on).
In "Save as type", choose "CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited) (*.csv)". Do not choose the similar "CSV (Comma delimited) (*.csv)".
Click Save. If you see "Some features might be lost", click Yes.

googleSheets.title: Google Sheets
steps: Choose File → Download → Comma-separated values (.csv). It is always UTF-8.

numbers.title: Numbers (Mac, iPhone, iPad)
steps: Under Advanced Options, set Text Encoding to "Unicode (UTF-8)" and export.

save.oldExcel: In older Excel versions without "CSV UTF-8", save as "Unicode Text (*.txt)" and choose that file as it is.
save.sheets: Only the sheet that is open is saved to the CSV. Open the sheet with your word table before saving.

strategyNotes.keepBoth: They are added as separate words. You can combine them later with "Organize duplicates".
strategyNotes.merge: Meanings, examples and tags from both are kept, so nothing is lost. The existing word's pronunciation and study progress take priority.

dup.title: Organize duplicates
dup.intro: These are groups of words with the same characters and the same pinyin (or no pinyin on one side). The selected groups are merged into one word each. Keeping duplicates does not cause any problems for studying.

rules.title: How words are merged
rules.reading: The word registered first keeps its pronunciation. If it is empty, the other word's value is used.
rules.progress: For each study mode, the record you studied most recently is kept. The other record is deleted.
rules.content: Both are kept (identical ones are combined).
